chunks: He said: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Al-Qassim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Ubays ibn Hisham an-Nashiri narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them).
And Imran al-Hamdani asked him, saying to him: May Allah make you succeed! Some people criticize us and say that you claim that there will be a voice from the heaven.
He said to him: Do not narrate from me, but narrate it from my father. My father used to say: It is in the Book of Allah.
(If We please, We should send down upon them a sign from the heaven so that their necks should stoop to it).

Then all the people of the earth will believe in the first call. When it is the next day, Iblis the accursed will rise high until he disappears from the earth into the sky's atmosphere, then he will call out: 'Indeed, Uthman has been killed unjustly, so seek vengeance for his blood.'
Then those whom Allah wills to go astray will return (to disbelief), and they will say: 'This is the magic of the Shia.' Until they accuse us and say: 'It is from their magic.'
(And if they see a miracle they turn aside and say: Transient magic).
And this is the saying of Allah.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the voice from heaven and the claim about Uthman in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the 'voice from heaven' is a specific eschatological sign preceding the Mahdi's appearance, where Iblis ascends to proclaim 'Uthman was killed unjustly' to deceive the masses. This event fulfills the Quranic description of those who see a clear sign yet dismiss it as 'persistent magic' (sihr mustamarr), causing a segment of believers to revert to error. The narration highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of this phenomenon as a test of faith where the truth is recognized but rejected due to political or tribal allegiances.
